neighbours.label: ' the' introducing a specific referent as object of a verb in explanatory prose (often body / biology)
fire: After a meal, the pancreas releases insulin so cells can take up the glucose in the blood.
The liver stores the extra sugar as glycogen for later use.
During exercise, muscles burn the fat that is stored around them.
White blood cells attack the bacteria that enter a wound.
The kidneys regulate the salt balance of the body.
When we fast, the body breaks down the protein in muscle.
Red blood cells carry the oxygen from the lungs to tissues.
The small intestine absorbs the nutrients from digested food.
quiet: After a meal, the pancreas releases insulin so cells can take up glucose from blood.
The liver stores extra sugar as glycogen for later use.
During exercise, muscles burn fat that is stored around them.
White blood cells attack bacteria that enter a wound.
Kidneys regulate salt balance in our bodies.
When we fast, our bodies break down protein in muscle.
Red blood cells carry oxygen from lungs to tissues.
Small intestines absorb nutrients from digested food.

notes: 31 of 32 top examples peak on ' the', mostly after a verb or preposition in explanations (respond to the hormone, converts food to glucose, the simple sugar). The + pole is also ' the' (idioms: to the last minute), so the distinction is unclear. Probe: 0.92 'absorb the sugar', 0.14 'opened the door'.
